'''Senami Haguro Shrine''' is a shrine in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Echigo Province]].

'''Senami Haguro Shrine''' (西奈彌羽黒神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} located in {{ill|Murakami, Niigata|ja|村上市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Niigata Prefecture|ja|新潟県|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Along with {{ill|Senami Shrine|ja|西奈彌神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in Senami Hamamachi, it is considered a possible location of the "Senami Shrine" mentioned in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|ja|延喜式神名帳|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|qq=draft|qq=draft}} as a shrine of {{ill|Echigo Province|ja|越後国磐船郡|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. The former shrine Ranking was {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Locally, it is simply called '''Haguro Shrine'''.

The original deity enshrined was Natsu-hime no Ōkami, and later, Ukanomitama no Mikoto and Tsukuyomi no Mikoto were added from {{ill|Dewa Sanzan|ja|出羽三山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. During the Edo period, the shrine was known as "Haguro Sansho Gongen." Natsu-hime no Kami is believed to be the daughter of {{ill|Hayamato|ja|羽戸山命|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, the grandson of {{ill|Susanoo|ja|スサノオ|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and is considered the deity who developed the area.

== History ==
The shrine was established in the first year of {{ill|Empress Jitō|ja|持統天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (687 AD) and was originally located at the summit of Mount Senami.

During the {{ill|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|ja|天正|lt=Tenshō Era|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (1573–1592), {{ill|Honjō Shigenaga|ja|本庄繁長|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, who ruled the area, went to the aid of the {{ill|Daibōji clan|ja|大宝寺氏|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in Dewa Shōnai, leading to conflict with the {{ill|Mogami clan|ja|最上氏|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and the Tōzenji clan (vassals of the Daibōji). Shigenaga prayed at the {{ill|Dewa Shrine|ja|出羽神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and, after his victory, enshrined part of its deity in Senami Haguro Shrine. The shrine then became the region’s main shrine. Later, under the rule of {{ill|Murakami Tadakatsu|ja|村上忠勝|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, the shrine was relocated from the summit to its current location midway up Mount Senami.

Despite the transition from the Honjō to the {{ill|Hori clan|ja|堀氏|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, the shrine continued to receive veneration. {{ill|Hori Naomune|ja|堀直寄|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, who renovated {{ill|Murakami Castle|ja|村上城|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, built a three-story keep that overlooked the shrine. Finding this disrespectful, he ordered the shrine relocated to its present site in 1632 (Kan'ei 10). At this time, the shrine adopted the name "Haguro Sansho Gongen." The relocation date was recorded as the 7th day of the 6th lunar month, which became the annual festival date. After Japan adopted the solar calendar in the Meiji era, the festival was shifted to July 7.

In 1870 (Meiji 3), the shrine was renamed to its current name. In 1894 (Meiji 27), it was designated a Gōsha (village shrine), and in 1928 (Shōwa 3), it was promoted to a {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.

== Major Annual Events ==
* {{ill|Murakami Grand Festival|ja|村上大祭|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (July 7)

== location and Access ==
Senami Haguro Shrine is located in the southern part of Murakami city, midway up Mount Sankyo.

; Transportation
* 3-minute walk from the "Hagurocho" bus stop on the Murakami City Loop Bus.
